summary: The combined f6bd7d8b evaluation now emits all 138 screens and leaves 5 unmatched. The former planning-clone map_invisible() exception is gone. The first residual difference is a monster-turn RNG call-order split at step 133: C enters distfleeck() while JavaScript reaches resist_conflict(). C source places distfleeck() in dochug() before and after its movement branch; JavaScript has the corresponding range checks and phase-four gate. source.branch: dochug() runs distfleeck() before the movement decision and recalculates it after m_move() when that movement phase ran; the standard Conflict/resist_conflict() attack gate follows. The observed C and JavaScript calls reach those source-owned checks in different order, but the saved evidence does not expose the monster or state that selected the path.

evidence: Current combined evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261003200023-v21.json was produced at f6bd7d8b254913e53e05ca7fd0a7048eed7f8f34. Its Archon case record reports 133/138 screens, 2711/2820 RNG calls, and 137/138 cursors matched, leaving 5 unmatched screens.

The assigned-case scan /tmp/teleport-validation-1000/run-XaRRJG/stdout.log at replay commit c0f096740f8cafb9776647704f60947cef25fe74 reports the same 133/138 screen boundary at segment 0 step 133. At RNG index 2705, C is rn2(5)=1 from distfleeck(monmove.c:538) and JS is rnd(20)=12; the differing status cells show C HP 3 and JS HP 1. The parent confirmed that the combined f6bd7d8b helper is equivalent and that the full current evaluation retains this case at 133/138.

The C recording step 133 has this order at its start: rnd(3)=3 in gazemu, rn2(5)=4 attributed to dochug, rn2(5)=1 in distfleeck, rnd(20)=20 in resist_conflict, a second rn2(5)=4 in distfleeck, then mattacku/hitmu and knockback calls. This proves the C ordering for the recorded turn but does not identify the monster instance at each call or the matching JavaScript actor.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/monmove.c:790-791 calls distfleeck() before item actions; :910-915 calls m_move() and recalculates distfleeck() when movement did not kill the monster; :965-968 evaluates the phase-four Conflict/resist_conflict() gate. JavaScript js/monmove.js:2603 calls distanceAndFear() before phase three, its mayMove block recalculates it after moveMonster(), and :2763-2769 contains the phase-four resist_conflict() gate. This identifies monmove.c:dochug() as the current source owner; the saved scan cannot distinguish a mayMove predicate/state difference from an m_move() result or monster iteration-order difference.

The step-133 Archon knockback path is counter-evidence for treating the old dothrow.c finding as the current cause: C uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback() first draws knock distance at :5258 and then returns at :5269-5270 when rn2(chance) is nonzero; this recording has rn2(6)=3, so it exits before attack eligibility or hurtle(). At step 135, rn2(6)=0 only opens later gates and does not prove hurtle_step() executes.

The previous stop was the planning-clone TypeError map_invisible() draws to the global game in dothrow.c:hurtle_step(), recorded in the prior investigation at ee3dc7db5cacad4d18557379dd75b9558de8d421. The old branch correction is no longer the first unresolved behavior; retain it only as resolved counter-evidence.
